summary_paragraph: Mrs. ___ was readmitted for failure to thrive, fever, productive cough, and worsening abdominal pain around her gastrostomy tube. She had been recently discharged after a prior admission for radiation-induced esophagitis and G-tube placement. Imaging revealed new right lower lobe consolidation consistent with healthcare-associated pneumonia, for which she was treated with intravenous vancomycin and cefepime. Her abdominal pain and feed leakage were attributed to a mechanical issue with the pigtail G-tube, which was successfully replaced with a balloon-type MIC feeding tube, leading to marked improvement. Her esophagitis was managed with lansoprazole and oral rest, and her chronic pain was controlled with morphine while discontinuing sedating medications like nortriptyline. She completed antibiotic therapy, showed clinical resolution of infection, and was discharged to an extended care facility for rehabilitation with plans for outpatient GI and rheumatology follow-up.
